label: August 1885
atlas_dek: The episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1885 from our dossiers, our first month from the 1880s, placed on 1910 county lines and by month (some July events were first reported in August). Hover for a short summary; select a dot to read the account in the sidebar. Drafts: no entry has had human review.
reader_intro:
Dossiers for 31 episodes of anti-Black violence reported in August 1885, our first month from the 1880s. They come from the 44 events in the August 1885 table, which includes July events first reported in August. We did not write dossiers for 17 events with non-Black victims, for duplicates, or for events plainly out of scope. Searches covered August papers, plus September papers for more on known episodes.

Thirteen of the 44 dossiers are set aside. Four are duplicates folded into another record: the Ross and Prewitt shootings at Canton, Texas; one of the two Waterloo reports; and the Gorin warning in Humphreys County. Nine are out of scope. In five, no report gives the victim's race: Huffman, Fowler, Diana Brown, Halbrook, Addie King. Two were routine arrests (Gus Johnson, John Hunt), one was a two-sided fight (Archie Green), and the Asbury Park color-line campaign involved no force.

Method: a research agent (Sonnet) searched Black and white papers. A write-up agent (Opus) wrote the dossier with keyed citations, and a code check confirmed every quote and citation against the article text. Black-press clippings are shown as page images and white-press articles as text. For 1885 the Black press is thin: the main Black paper is the New York Freeman, which is still counted under the white press in our sources (LoC pages).

Drafts: no entry has had human review.
